belief: My clothes, car, or home show my worth.
origins: Appearances can feel like a language everyone reads. A parent who dressed up for the neighbors, a school where brands mattered, or a workplace where the car in the parking lot sent a message can teach us to treat possessions as proof of value. This can lead to overspending, quiet shame about what we lack, or judgment of others by what they own.
teaches: God told Samuel, “For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” Peter writes that true beauty should not come from outward adornment such as fine clothes, but from the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God’s sight. Jesus said that the poor widow put in more than all the others, because she gave out of her poverty all she had. Our worth is not displayed on the outside.
self_statements: People judge me by what I drive.
If my house looks small, so am I.
I have to dress the part to be taken seriously.
Nice things prove I have made it.
Having less shows I am less.
I would be embarrassed if people saw my home.
errors: Assuming people judge me by my things.
Feeling ashamed of my car and concluding I am less.
Treating possessions as a label for me.
Seeing myself as either impressive or a failure.
questions: What do I try to say with my clothes, car, or home?
Who am I trying to impress, and why?
What has the pressure to look successful cost me?
Whom do I admire, and is it for what they own?
What does God see when He looks at me?
What would change if I stopped performing with my possessions?
truth: God looks at my heart, not my possessions. My clothes, car, and home are tools and gifts, not a measure of my worth. I can enjoy what I have, keep it in its place, and let character speak for me.
hw_truths: My things do not show my worth.
A gentle spirit is precious to God.
I can enjoy my things without needing them.
I am enough without impressing anyone.
log: Each week, write one moment when you chose substance over appearance.
actions: List what you are trying to say.
Write the message you hope your possessions send.
Ask, “Is this for me or for the impression?”
Identify three people whose character you admire and what you admire.
Give something of value that nobody will see you give.
prayer: Lord, You look at the heart. Free me from needing my things to speak for me. Help me use what I have with thanks and let my character and kindness be my testimony. Amen.
hw_questions: What am I trying to say with my things?
Who am I trying to impress?
What has this pressure cost me?
Whom do I admire and why?
What does God see in me?
What could I do quietly instead of publicly?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The Lord looks at my heart, so my worth is not in my things.”
